profile.name: Prasandh Kishore P
profile.shortIntroduction: I build reliable .NET and Angular systems for complex, real-time, and hardware-integrated workflows.
longIntroduction: Senior Software Engineer with 5+ years of experience developing enterprise applications across web, desktop, client-server, and hardware-integrated environments. I specialize in full-stack development using C#, ASP.NET Core, Web API, Angular, React, Entity Framework Core, and WinForms.

At Everi, I work on next-generation kiosk and ATM-related systems, developing modular and plugin-based architectures, multi-threaded components, and hardware-integrated workflows. My experience includes designing RESTful and gRPC services, implementing real-time communication using SignalR, and building maintainable solutions following SOLID principles and clean architecture practices.

I have also worked closely with cross-functional teams, participated in system design discussions, peer programming, code reviews, and Agile delivery. I focus on solving complex engineering problems while building reliable, scalable, and maintainable software.

projects.title: Modular Kiosk Application Platform
projects.shortDescription: A sanitized case study on structuring reusable capabilities across hardware-integrated kiosk workflows.
projects.detailedDescription: A professional engineering case study focused on a modular application platform for complex kiosk workflows. Product-specific details are intentionally omitted; the case study highlights the architectural constraints, engineering responsibilities, and reusable patterns involved.
responsibilities: Developed and enhanced workflow capabilities across frontend and backend components.
Contributed to modular and plugin-based application boundaries.
Integrated UI, application services, and hardware-facing components.
Investigated state, communication, timeout, and integration issues across distributed components.
challenges: Keeping platform capabilities isolated while supporting shared workflows and hardware integrations.
Maintaining consistent state across UI, backend services, and device-facing components.
solutions: Applied modular service boundaries and reusable abstractions around shared capabilities.
Used structured communication contracts to reduce coupling between distributed components.
Separated workflow logic from device-specific integration concerns where possible.
outcomes: Improved reuse and maintainability across related workflows.
Created clearer extension points for additional platform capabilities.
Reduced the risk of changes in one integration affecting unrelated workflows.

projects.title: Real-Time Notification and Popup Layer
projects.shortDescription: A reusable SignalR-based communication approach for notifications and user decisions across application components.
projects.detailedDescription: A sanitized case study describing a reusable notification and popup mechanism for distributed application components. It focuses on message flow, user-response handling, and keeping UI behavior consistent without exposing proprietary implementation details.
responsibilities: Designed reusable UI and service abstractions for popup-driven workflows.
Integrated real-time notifications between backend and frontend components.
Handled user responses, timeout behavior, and state updates across asynchronous flows.
challenges: Correlating a notification with the correct workflow and user response.
Preventing stale or duplicate messages from leaving the UI in an inconsistent state.
Keeping the mechanism reusable across workflows with different presentation requirements.
solutions: Used typed message contracts and correlation identifiers for request-response flows.
Centralized popup orchestration and lifecycle handling instead of duplicating behavior in individual screens.
Applied explicit timeout and cleanup paths for asynchronous operations.
outcomes: Established more consistent popup behavior across multiple workflows.
Reduced duplicated notification and timeout handling code.
Made new popup-driven use cases easier to integrate.

projects.title: Reliable Workflow State Management
projects.shortDescription: A case study on handling timeouts, confirmations, rejection paths, and recovery in transaction-oriented interfaces.
projects.detailedDescription: A sanitized professional case study about keeping long-running, transaction-oriented workflows consistent when timeouts, user prompts, service responses, and hardware events can arrive asynchronously.
responsibilities: Implemented workflow states and transitions across UI and backend components.
Handled timeout, confirmation, rejection, and recovery scenarios.
Diagnosed race conditions and state inconsistencies in asynchronous flows.
challenges: Avoiding conflicting transitions when user actions, timers, and service events occur close together.
Returning the application to a predictable state after interruption or rejection.
Providing clear feedback while background processing is still active.
solutions: Defined explicit workflow states and guarded transitions between them.
Centralized timer cleanup and terminal-state handling.
Used real-time events to synchronize visible UI state with backend processing.
outcomes: Improved consistency across timeout- and confirmation-driven workflows.
Made edge cases easier to reason about, test, and troubleshoot.
Reduced the chance of a workflow remaining in an ambiguous state.
